newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Sobhraj has strong citizenship case.
newsitem.headline: France says Sobhraj has strong citizenship case.

text.p: France said on Monday it had "strong reasons" to believe that notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj, due to be deported from India to France on Tuesday, can legitimately claim French citizenship.
"Our checks have enabled us to dispel doubts about Mr Sobhraj's nationality," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said. "We have very strong reasons to believe that his nationality is French."
Sobhraj, who served 20 years in an Indian jail on a string of charges including murder and robbery, will arrive in Paris on Tuesday morning, ending months of uncertainty about his future.
Sobhraj has an Indian father and a Vietnamese mother, and claims French citizenship.
India ordered Sobhraj's deportation in February but France refused to accept him pending checks on his nationality claim.
France agreed on Friday to supply Sobhraj with a travel document that would allow him to enter the country.
Doutriaux said Sobhraj would have to apply for a certificate of citizenship, but indicated it would be a formality.
"It will be up to him to apply for a certificate of French nationality that will be granted by a judge," he said.

Sobhraj, whose exploits across Asia beginning in 1971 have been the subject of two books, was released from a high security prison on bail last month. He was immediately detained on the grounds that he lacked proper papers.
